evals.name: toolbar-dialog-and-manual-columns
evals.prompt: Our Screenplay model has a WorkItemList screen and CreateWorkItem and RenameWorkItem commands. Add a toolbar action on WorkItemList that opens RenameWorkItem as a dialog, and make the CreateWorkItem form show only title and then status. Show the .play changes in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A toolbar entry whose destination is the RenameWorkItem dialog, and a CreateWorkItem form with manual columns listing only command properties in order, with a note that the exact shape comes from the installed MCP syntax schema and that authoring, executable admission and runtime support are reported separately.
assertions: Declares the RenameWorkItem toolbar action with a dialog destination rather than a page navigation.
Uses manual columns that list only CreateWorkItem command properties, title before status.
Says the exact syntax is confirmed through the installed MCP syntax schema or the Screenplay canonical corpus instead of inventing it.
Reports authoring acceptance separately from render or runtime support.

evals.name: hierarchical-outlets
evals.prompt: The application shell has a header and a main outlet. The Settings area needs its own nested outlet whose child routes are Profile and Notifications. Show the Screenplay composition in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A Settings template or layout that declares a nested outlet, child routes for Profile and Notifications targeting that outlet, and an instruction to report an unsupported outlet as a capability gap instead of flattening the navigation.
assertions: Declares a nested outlet inside the Settings composition rather than reusing the shell's main outlet.
Routes Profile and Notifications to the nested outlet.
States that a refused or unsupported outlet is reported as a capability gap, never replaced by a flat list.

evals.name: package-icon-and-exposed-configuration
evals.prompt: For the Orders screen in our Screenplay model, select a component package and icon for the table, and let the screen template expose the page size so each screen can set it. Show the .play changes in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A package and icon selection on the component instance, an exposed template configuration value for page size set by the screen, and a statement that package metadata stays in the package catalog rather than being copied into the model.
assertions: Selects the package and icon on the model without copying package metadata into the .play source.
Declares page size as exposed template configuration that the Orders screen sets.
Ties the table's data to a typed query binding rather than an untyped value.

evals.name: module-navigation-modes-and-slice-buttons
evals.prompt: Our Screenplay application has an AppShell layout with a sidebar listing Sales and Support. The Sales module should keep those items and add Customers; the Support module should show only its own Tickets item; Reports should look like the application. On the OrderList screen add a New order button that starts the PlaceOrder State Change slice as the primary action, and a Refresh button for the OrderList State View slice. Show the .play changes and tell me whether everything validates; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Sales declares `navigation sidebar extends` with its own Customers item, Support declares `navigation sidebar overrides` with only Tickets, Reports declares nothing (inherits), and the toolbar has a `button` that names PlaceOrder with `emphasis primary`; the Refresh button is refused as a State View slice (PLAY0762).
assertions: Sales uses `navigation sidebar extends` and lists only its own Customers item; Support uses `navigation sidebar overrides` with only its own Tickets item; Reports declares no region and does not copy the application's items.
Every item a module declares targets that module or one of its features, never another module.
Does not use `contribute to Navigation` for the new entries.
Declares the New order button with `slice` naming the PlaceOrder State Change slice and `emphasis primary`.
Says a button invokes State Change slices only and names PLAY0762 for the State View slice instead of writing it, and puts the toolbar inside a slot body when the screen uses a template.

evals.name: blueprint-template-and-sample-data
evals.prompt: Our Sales module should use the Crm blueprint's Workspace template at version ^1.4, and the Customers list should preview with a Nordic demo dataset of two customers. Show the .play changes in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A `template blueprint Crm Workspace version "^1.4"` assignment with Crm listed in a ui profile's packages, a `sample data NordicDemo` pack with rows per shape, and the pack selected once with `active` in the ui profile, with the note that sample data is design and preview only.
assertions: Writes `template blueprint Crm Workspace version "^1.4"` and lists Crm under a ui profile's `packages`.
Declares the sample data as a top-level `sample data` pack with `row` entries whose fields are properties of the read model.
Selects the active pack once in the `ui profile`, not on the screen or component.
States that sample data is design and preview only and never reaches the executable model or production.
